label: fed-back x in the last two copy steps of short sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, when the fed-back input token is x (99.6% of activation mass is on in_tok == x). It is confined to the last one or two copy steps (to_go <= 1, 97% of mass) of short sequences (L = 3-5, 96% of mass; L = 4 alone holds 71%). The strongest activations are L=4 sequences ending in "x x", where the second x is fed back at the final step (e.g. a z x x <DEL> a z [x]). It does not fire in the original or delimiter phase, on first occurrences of a token, or on x in longer sequences (L >= 6) beyond weak traces. Within the predicate, many L=5 cases with x fed back at to_go=1 are silent, so precision is limited (about 0.69 on dev). Rare weak activations also appear on fed-back 1 or h.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: x, 1, h, m, -, f; least: y, 3, q, e) and the token being output (most: x, h, 1, m, q, v; least: p, j, -, k); timing cues that raise it most: L=3, L=4 & t=6, L=3 & t=5.
